lines: Okay friend, here's the whole sermon in one box. Jesus flips the world upside down: the poor, the hungry and the weeping are blessed, and the rich, the well fed and the ones laughing now hear "woe" (Luke 6:20-26).

Then He asks for the hardest thing in the recipe: love your enemies, give without keeping score, lend expecting nothing in return. Why? Because that's what God is like. "He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked" (Luke 6:35).

No scoreboard. No receipts. No "remember when I helped you move?" Just "Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful" (Luke 6:36). And the measure you use is the measure that comes back to you (Luke 6:38).

And before you go fixing anybody's speck, check your own eye for a BEAM (Luke 6:41-42). Trust me, friend. I stamped crooked for YEARS. I am the LAST stamper who should be inspecting other people's cookies.
Because what's inside is what comes out. A tree is known by its fruit, and "out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks" (Luke 6:44-45).

So here's the big idea: hearing isn't enough, and calling Him "Lord, Lord" isn't enough. The one who hears His words and acts on them builds on the rock, and when the torrent hits, that house doesn't shake (Luke 6:46-49).
Reading the recipe and baking the recipe are two VERY different things. Ask anybody who's read the instructions twice and still burned the batch.
